title: The Stretchable and Noise‐Resistant Cables for Connection of Soft Electronics
abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible electronics with excellent adaptivity to soft tissue have been successfully developed based on the efforts of materials and devices, but the cables for connection of soft electronics are easily overlooked. Xinge Yu and colleagues reported that multi‐scale, recyclable three‐dimensional stretchable core–shell cables (3D‐SCSC) can not only serve as electrically and mechanically reliable interconnects among various soft/rigid/hybrid electronic components but also provide a fundamental platform for the materials design of customized cables.

title: Recyclable and Leakage-Resistant Phase Change Materials with Reversible Solid-Gel Transition
authors: Shuai Fan; Kongying Zhu; Xiaoyan Yuan; Lixia Ren
abstract: Abstract Phase change materials (PCMs) are critical for thermal management but are prone to leakage in the molten state. Cross-linked polymer networks can effectively encapsulate PCMs, but increasing cross-linking density progressively compromises their latent heat. Herein, we present a facile strategy for encapsulating methoxy polyethylene glycol (mPEG) in a reversible solid-gel transition network with tunable cross-linking density. Taking advantage of the high reactivity between anhydride and amino groups, the cross-linking density of the network can be regulated, allowing the minimum network constraint required for leakage resistance while maximizing the mPEG content and latent heat storage capacity. The resulting PCM achieves a high latent heat value of 143.7 J/g with mPEG loading of 97 wt %. Meanwhile, the dynamic and reversible intermolecular interactions within the network endow the material with excellent leakage resistance and recyclability. After at least 50 grinding-reshaping cycles, both leakage resistance and enthalpy remain essentially unchanged. In the thermal management test, a temperature difference of 8.5 °C is achieved between inside and outside of the model during the heating process. During the cooling process, a constant-temperature plateau lasting 50 min is observed. Benefiting from these advantages, the material exhibits promising prospects for thermal management applications.

title: Preparation and Properties of Deep Eutectic Solvent-Modified Soy Protein and Soy Protein–Chitosan Composite Films
authors: Huachun Qi; Xiaoqi Wang; Yuetong Lin; Honggang Zhao; Jiuyin Pang; Yaoxing Sun
abstract: Conventional non-biodegradable plastic packaging causes severe environmental pollution, driving the demand for degradable biomass food packaging. Chitosan (CS) is an ideal green film material but suffers weak mechanical, water-resistance and antioxidant properties. Soy protein isolate (SPI) is cheap and abundant; however, its compact molecular structure leads to poor miscibility with pure CS. Herein, ultrasonic-assisted deep eutectic solvent (DES) pretreatment was used to unfold SPI’s protein structure and release active sites for stronger SPI–CS interfacial interactions. Citric acid and transglutaminase (TG) served as dual green crosslinkers, while carvacrol (Car) and gallic acid (GA) were added as natural polyphenol antioxidants. Single-factor and Box–Behnken response surface experiments determined the optimal film-forming parameters: a citric acid mass ratio of 0.84, a TG dosage of 2.60 U∙g−1, and a drying temperature of 65 °C. The optimized DES–SPI–CS film possessed a tensile strength of 18.79 MPa and an elongation at break of 41.39%, with greatly enhanced water resistance and thermal stability. After co-loading Car and GA, the composite film reached 79.33% DPPH radical-scavenging activity. Twelve-day cherry tomato preservation tests confirmed its capacity to slow vitamin C loss and fruit decay. This work provides a sustainable integrated strategy combining DES modification, dual crosslinking and natural antioxidant doping to fabricate multifunctional bio-based packaging, offering theoretical support for biodegradable film substitution of disposable plastics.
